items.title: Creating and Updating
items.intent: New or changed documented information has identification, suitable format and media, and review and approval for suitability, by identified authorized persons.
items.question: Show a recent maintenance document: its identification, format, review, and the authorized approver.
evidence: Document with title, date, author or reference, and approval record
List of authorized approvers by document type
failure_modes: Document approved by someone not authorized

items.title: Control of Documented Information
items.intent: Documented information is controlled as a set.
items.question: How do you control maintenance documents as a set?

items.title: Availability and protection
items.intent: Documented information is available where and when needed and protected from loss, improper use and loss of integrity.
items.question: Show where the current maintenance data is available at the point of work, and how it is protected.
evidence: Protection controls such as backups and permissions
failure_modes: Current maintenance data not available at point of work

items.title: Distribution, storage, change, retention and obsolete documents
items.intent: Control covers distribution, storage, version control, retention, prevention of obsolete use, external documents, electronic data protection, and notifying authors of inaccurate or ambiguous maintenance data in time.
items.question: How do you stop obsolete maintenance data being used, and how do you tell the author about an error in the data?
evidence: Record of notification to the author of inaccurate or ambiguous data
failure_modes: Errors in maintenance data not reported to the author

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Operational Planning and Control
items.intent: Maintenance processes are planned and controlled: requirements, criteria, resources, documented evidence, the use and maintenance support of the product, outsourced work, controls to prevent delivery of nonconforming work, and critical maintenance tasks.
items.question: Walk me through how you plan and control one maintenance job from requirement to release, including any critical task.
evidence: Work order or quality plan for a sample job

items.title: Operational Risk Management
items.intent: Operational risks are assigned, assessed, communicated, mitigated, and accepted against defined criteria.
items.question: Show your operational risk process: who owns it, how risks are assessed, and how a risk above your acceptance criteria was handled.
failure_modes: Risks above criteria accepted without formal decision

items.title: Configuration Management
items.intent: Products are delivered in the approved configuration, and traceability of requirements to the product, design and operational attributes is controlled.
items.question: Pick an aircraft component: show it is delivered in the approved configuration and how requirements are traced to it.
evidence: Traceability of requirements to the product
failure_modes: Product delivered in a configuration different from the approved one

items.title: Product Safety
items.intent: Product safety is assured through hazard identification (reactive and proactive), risk analysis, managing changes that affect safety, assessing the safety processes, training, communication of safety information, and reporting safety events to customer, authority and type certificate holder.
items.question: Show how a hazard is identified, how a safety event was reported, and what staff were trained on product safety.
evidence: Safety event report to customer or authority
failure_modes: Safety event not reported to required parties

items.title: Prevention of Counterfeit Parts
items.intent: Counterfeit or suspect counterfeit parts are kept out of delivered work through training, authorized sourcing, traceability and verification.
items.question: Show how a part is sourced from an authorized source and verified, and how a suspect part would be quarantined.

items.title: Prevention of Suspected Unapproved Parts
items.intent: Unapproved and suspected unapproved parts are identified and kept out of use, through training, traceable procurement to an authorized source, inspection, and quarantine and reporting.
items.question: Show how you check incoming parts for approval status, and what you did the last time a suspected unapproved part was found.
evidence: Incoming inspection record for approval status

items.title: Installation of Approved Parts
items.intent: Approved parts are properly identified, acceptable for the product, in satisfactory condition with airworthiness directives complied with, within life limits, handled correctly if removed from an accident or incident aircraft, and dismantled only by an organization holding the required approvals.
items.question: Pick one installed part: show its identification, airworthiness directive status, life-limit status, and the approvals of any organization that dismantled it.

items.title: Requirements for Products and Services
items.intent: Customer product and service requirements are understood and agreed before commitment.
items.question: Show how a maintenance requirement is captured and agreed before you accept the work.

items.title: Customer Communication
items.intent: Customer communication covers product information, enquiries and orders, feedback and complaints, customer property, and contingency requirements.
items.question: Show how a customer complaint about maintenance work was captured and handled.

items.title: Determining the Requirements for Products and Services
items.intent: Maintenance requirements are defined including statutory and regulatory requirements, the organization can meet its claims, special requirements are determined, and operational risks such as ability to deliver on time are identified.
items.question: For one maintenance capability you offer, show the defined requirements and the risks you identified.
failure_modes: Claims made that the organization cannot meet

items.title: Review of the Requirements for Products and Services
items.intent: A review happens before commitment, covering customer, implied, organizational, regulatory and changed requirements, with technical data at the contractual revision.
items.question: Show a recent work order review, and how it confirmed the technical data revision.
failure_modes: Work performed to an out-of-date data revision

items.title: Review before commitment
items.intent: Before commitment, the organization confirms it can meet requirements, negotiates any it cannot meet, resolves changed requirements, and has a process for disposition of out-of-scope defects found during maintenance.
items.question: Show a case where an out-of-scope defect was found during maintenance, and how it was dispositioned with the customer.
failure_modes: Out-of-scope defect worked without customer agreement

items.title: Retained review results
items.intent: Review results and new requirements are kept.
items.question: Where are your review results kept?

items.title: Changes to Requirements for Products and Services
items.intent: When requirements change, documents are amended and affected people are told.
items.question: Show a recent requirement change: which documents changed and who was informed.
failure_modes: Documents not amended after a change

items.title: Design and Development of Products and Services
items.intent: Where authorized, technical data such as repair data and maintenance programmes are developed under a controlled process. Where the organization does not do this, the exclusion is documented in the quality manual.
items.question: Do you develop any repair data or maintenance programmes? If not, where is that exclusion recorded and justified?
evidence: Process for developing technical data where authorized
Quality manual exclusion record where not performed
failure_modes: Repair data developed without authorization or process

items.title: General
items.intent: A design and development process exists where needed, and for repair data it covers classification, description and evidence of approval.
items.question: Show the process for developing repair data, including its classification and evidence of approval.
evidence: Repair data record with classification and approval evidence
failure_modes: Repair data without classification or approval evidence

items.title: Design and Development Planning
items.intent: Design and development stages, reviews, verification and validation, responsibilities, resources, interfaces, customer involvement, and documentation are planned.
items.question: For one development project, show the plan with stages, reviews and verification.

items.title: Design and Development Inputs
items.intent: Inputs include functional and performance requirements, regulatory requirements, applicable standards, consequences of failure, and all continuing airworthiness requirements, and conflicts are resolved.
items.question: Show the inputs to one repair design, including the continuing airworthiness requirements, and how conflicts were resolved.
evidence: Design input record with continuing airworthiness requirements

items.title: Design and Development Controls
items.intent: Design results are defined, reviewed, verified, validated, problems acted on, and documented.
items.question: Walk me through one repair design review and its verification and validation.

items.title: Design and Development Outputs
items.intent: Outputs meet inputs, are adequate for later processes, include monitoring and acceptance criteria, identify essential characteristics, and define the data needed to use and maintain the product, with outputs incorporated into work orders for maintenance programmes.
items.question: Show the outputs of one repair design, and how they were incorporated into the work order.
failure_modes: Outputs not incorporated into the work order

items.title: Design and Development Changes
items.intent: Design changes are identified, reviewed, controlled, customers are notified before implementation where required, and changes are controlled under configuration management.
items.question: Show the last repair design change: its review, authorization and customer notification.
failure_modes: Change implemented without review or notification

items.title: Control of Externally Provided Processes, Products, and Services
items.intent: Externally provided processes, products and services conform, and providers are controlled according to their approval status and impact.
items.question: Show how you control one external provider, from approval status through to performance review.
failure_modes: Provider used without approval status recorded

items.title: General
items.intent: External provision is controlled, including approved or customer-designated sources, risk, criteria for evaluation and selection, monitoring and re-evaluation.
items.question: How do you evaluate, select, monitor and re-evaluate external providers, including those the customer specified?

items.title: External provider approval and register
items.intent: Approval status decisions, changes and controlled use are defined; a register holds approval status and scope; performance is reviewed; actions for providers that do not meet requirements are defined; and product safety principles are flowed down.
items.question: Show your provider register with approval status and scope, the last performance review, and the flow-down of product safety principles to one provider.
evidence: Provider register with approval status and scope
failure_modes: Register missing approval status or scope
Product safety principles not flowed down

items.title: Type and Extent of Control
items.intent: External work does not weaken delivery of conforming work. Controls on the provider and the output are set according to impact, the provider holds required approvals, non-certificated providers are qualified and overseen, and verification is risk-based.
items.question: For one external provider, show its required approvals, how a non-certificated provider was qualified, and the risk-based verification you applied to its output.
evidence: Approval and certificate of the provider
Qualification and oversight record for a non-certificated provider

items.title: Information for External Providers
items.intent: Requirements are adequate and sent to providers, covering processes, approvals, competence, performance control, verification, flow-down, notifications of nonconformity and change, access rights, product safety awareness, and the format of the delivery documentation package, and the conditions for reporting malfunctions, defects and unairworthy conditions.
items.question: Show the purchasing information sent to one provider, including the delivery documentation format and the conditions for reporting unairworthy conditions.
evidence: Reporting conditions for malfunctions, defects and unairworthy conditions
failure_modes: No reporting conditions for unairworthy conditions

items.title: Production and Service Provision
items.intent: Maintenance and service are carried out under controlled conditions.
items.question: Show how maintenance is carried out under controlled conditions for one job.
failure_modes: Work performed without controlled maintenance data

items.title: Control of Production and Service Provision
items.intent: Work is controlled through: defined characteristics and results from current maintenance data, monitoring and measurement, suitable infrastructure, competent persons, validation of processes that cannot be fully verified, human error prevention, release, in-process inspection points, evidence that all operations were completed, foreign object control, continuity of information at work handover, utilities, compliance with reference standards and technical data, management of approved capabilities and ratings, and control of work done away from the fixed location.
items.question: Pick one maintenance job and show: current maintenance data, in-process inspection points, the record that every operation was completed, handover continuity, and control of any work done off site.
evidence: Work order with current maintenance data
failure_modes: Work performed to superseded maintenance data

items.title: Control of Equipment, Tools, and Software Programs
items.intent: Equipment, tools and programs are those defined in the technical data or shown to be equivalent, equipment used to accept work is calibrated, and storage requirements with condition checks are defined.
items.question: For one task, show the tooling was the tooling defined in the technical data, and that the acceptance equipment is calibrated.
evidence: Tool list against the technical data
failure_modes: Non-specified tool used without demonstrated equivalence

items.title: Validation and Control of Special Processes
items.intent: Special processes are approved, conditions maintained, facilities and people qualified, methods defined, and records kept, including for outsourced special processes.
items.question: Show the approval and qualification for one special process, and its records of conditions maintained.
evidence: Qualification records of facilities and people
failure_modes: Special process run without approval or qualified people

items.title: Production Process Verification
items.intent: The licensed text marks this clause as not applicable for maintenance. The auditor confirms that the quality manual records this exclusion and its basis.
items.question: The standard text marks this clause not applicable. Show where your quality manual records that exclusion and why it applies to your scope.
evidence: Quality manual exclusion record for 8.5.1.3 with basis
Confirmation that no production work is performed
failure_modes: Exclusion not in the quality manual
items.note: Licensed text reads 'Production Process Verification (not applicable)'. Under the audit rule this is not an automatic N/A; it needs a quality-manual exclusion.

items.title: Evaluation of a New Capability
items.intent: Before the first article or product of a new capability, documentation, qualified people and tooling are evaluated, and results are submitted to the competent authority where required for the capability list.
items.question: Show the evaluation done before your first repair under a new capability, and any submission to the authority.
evidence: Evaluation record covering documentation, people and tooling
Submission to the competent authority where required

items.title: Identification and Traceability
items.intent: Outputs are identified, their configuration and inspection status are known, acceptance media are controlled, and traceability is kept where required.
items.question: Pick an aircraft component in work: show its identification, configuration, inspection status and traceability.
evidence: Identification on the item or traveler

items.title: Property Belonging to Customers or External Providers
items.intent: Customer property, including articles being maintained, is identified, verified, protected and safeguarded, and any loss or damage is reported to the owner.
items.question: Show how an aircraft or component owned by the customer is identified and protected while in your facility, and what was reported when some was found damaged.
evidence: Report of loss or damage to the customer
failure_modes: Customer article damaged and not reported

items.title: Preservation
items.intent: Outputs are preserved through identification, handling, contamination control, packaging, storage and transport, including cleaning, foreign object prevention, marking, shelf life and hazardous materials as they apply.
items.question: Show how a maintained component is preserved from completion to dispatch, including shelf-life control.

items.title: Post-Delivery Activities
items.intent: Post-delivery obligations are met, taking account of regulatory requirements, possible undesired consequences, customer feedback and occurrence reports. Problems found after delivery are investigated and reported.
items.question: Show a problem reported after delivery: how it was investigated and reported.

items.title: Control of Changes
items.intent: Production and service changes are reviewed, controlled, the persons who authorize them are identified, and review results are kept.
items.question: Show the last change to maintenance processes, its review, and the named person who authorized it.
evidence: List of persons authorized to approve changes

items.title: Release of Products and Services
items.intent: Release is not made until planned verification is complete. The authorized person signs the release documents only when all maintenance and inspection operations are complete per the contract and technical data, with no known nonconformity that endangers flight safety, and all required documentation accompanies the product.
items.question: Show a release certificate: the verification it relies on, the authorized signatory, and the documents that travel with the aircraft or component.
failure_modes: Release signed with known nonconformity open
Release by a person not authorized

items.title: Control of Nonconforming Outputs
items.intent: Nonconforming outputs are identified and controlled. Disposition is by the responsible person, containment is applied, customers are informed, and acceptance under concession is authorized by the competent authority and customer where needed. Unsalvageable and counterfeit parts are marked or controlled.
items.question: Show one nonconforming item in maintenance: how it was identified, contained, dispositioned, and who authorized any concession.
evidence: Competent authority or customer authorization for concession
failure_modes: Concession without competent authority or customer authorization

items.title: Nonconforming outputs control process
items.intent: The nonconformity control process is documented: responsibility and approval of disposition, containment, timely reporting to customers and relevant parties, and corrective action for problems found after delivery.
items.question: Show the documented nonconformity process and an example of timely reporting to a customer.
evidence: Customer or type certificate holder notification record

items.title: Retained nonconformity information
items.intent: Records describe the nonconformity, the actions, any concession, and the authority that decided.
items.question: Show the record for one nonconformity, its actions, any concession, and the deciding authority.

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis, and Evaluation
items.intent: The organization decides what to monitor and measure, the methods, and when to analyse and evaluate, and evaluates QMS and product safety performance.
items.question: Show what you monitor and what the analysis of the last period changed.

items.title: General
items.intent: The QMS and the safety performance related to products and services are evaluated, with records kept.
items.question: Show the evaluation of QMS and safety performance for the last period.

items.title: Customer Satisfaction
items.intent: Customer perceptions are monitored, including conformity, on-time delivery, complaints and corrective action requests, improvement plans address deficiencies, and plans do not conflict with the product safety policy.
items.question: How do you collect customer perception on maintenance, and what did you change because of it?
failure_modes: Improvement plan conflicts with safety policy

items.title: Analysis and Evaluation
items.intent: Monitoring data is analysed to evaluate conformity, satisfaction, QMS effectiveness, planning, risk actions, providers, improvement needs, product safety management, and opportunities to prevent maintenance error.
items.question: Show the analysis that looked at maintenance error prevention and product safety last period, and what it led to.
evidence: Analysis report covering the required areas

items.title: Internal Audit
items.intent: Internal audits run at planned intervals and show whether the QMS conforms to the organization's requirements and the standard, and is effectively implemented.
items.question: Show your internal audit programme and the last audit's findings and follow-up.

items.title: Internal audit scope
items.intent: Audits check conformity to the organization's requirements and the standard, and effective implementation.
items.question: For your last internal audit, show the criteria and the conclusion on effective implementation.

items.title: Audit programme and conduct
items.intent: The audit programme sets frequency, methods, responsibilities, planning and reporting, considering process importance, change and previous results. Each audit has criteria and scope, auditors are objective and impartial, results go to management, corrective action is timely, and records are kept.
items.question: Show the audit programme, how auditors were kept impartial, and how results were reported to management.

items.title: Management Review
items.intent: Top management reviews the QMS at planned intervals, including the need for changes to the safety policy and objectives.
items.question: Show the most recent management review, its attendees, and whether safety policy changes were considered.
failure_modes: Safety policy not considered in review

items.title: General
items.intent: Management reviews the QMS for continuing suitability, adequacy, effectiveness and strategic alignment, including the safety policy.
items.question: What is your planned review interval and when did the last review happen?
failure_modes: Review not held at planned intervals

items.title: Management Review Inputs
items.intent: The review considers earlier actions, changes in context, QMS performance trends (customers, objectives, process performance, nonconformities, measurement, audits, providers, on-time delivery), resources, risk actions, improvement opportunities, product safety monitoring, training effectiveness, and future changes to authority and customer requirements.
items.question: Show the inputs to the last review and confirm each required area was covered, including safety performance and training.
evidence: Management review input pack covering each required area
failure_modes: Safety performance not in the input pack

items.title: Management Review Outputs
items.intent: Outputs include decisions and actions on improvement, QMS changes, resources and risks, and results are kept.
items.question: Show the actions from the last review and their owners.
evidence: Review outputs with actions and owners

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: General
items.intent: Improvement opportunities are selected and acted on to meet customer requirements and enhance satisfaction, including product improvement, correction and prevention, QMS performance, and safety management performance.
items.question: Show two improvement actions from the last year, including one on safety management.

items.title: Nonconformity and Corrective Action
items.intent: Corrective action is managed: nonconformities are controlled and corrected, causes including human factors are found and removed, similar nonconformities are checked, effectiveness is reviewed, and the process is documented.
items.question: Pick one nonconformity: show the containment, the root cause including human factors, the corrective action, and the effectiveness review.
evidence: Corrective action record with root cause including human factors
failure_modes: Human factors not considered in root cause

items.title: Corrective action process
items.intent: After a nonconformity, the organization reacts and corrects it, deals with consequences, finds causes including human factors, checks for similar nonconformities, implements and reviews corrective action, updates risks and the QMS, flows requirements to providers responsible, and takes specific action when corrective action is late or ineffective.
items.question: Show the corrective action for one nonconformity from reaction to effectiveness review, and what you did when it was late.
evidence: Corrective action record through all steps
Flow-down to a provider where responsible
Escalation record for a late action
failure_modes: Corrective action closed without effectiveness review

items.title: Corrective action records
items.intent: Records show the nature of the nonconformities, actions taken, and the results of corrective action.
items.question: Show the records for one corrective action.

items.title: Continual Improvement
items.intent: The QMS suitability, adequacy and effectiveness are continually improved, using analysis, evaluation and management review outputs, and improvement activities are checked for effect.
items.question: Show an improvement from the last management review and how you checked it worked.
